proof_summary: Set \(N=201886\cdot3^{39101}-1\), so \(N+1=2\cdot100943\cdot3^{39101}\); modular computations with \(2+\sqrt3\) in the quadratic ring modulo \(N\) give a Lucas certificate of full order \(N+1\), using the three prime divisors \(2,100943,3\), and hence prove \(N\) prime. Thus the positive exponent \(39101\) supplies a counterexample to the proposed zero value.
